content.content: 1 --- 2 title: connection 3 description: API Reference for the connection function. 4 --- 5 6 The `connection()` function allows you to indicate rendering should wait for an incoming user request before continuing. 7 8 It's useful when a component doesn't use [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) like `cookies` or `headers`, but still needs to produce different output per request, such as `Math.random()` or `new Date()`. 9 10 ```ts filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 11 import { connection } from 'next/server' 12 13 export default async function Page() { 14 await connection() // prerendering stops here 15 // the following code only runs at request time 16 const rand = Math.random() 17 return {rand} 18 } 19 ``` 20 21 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 22 import { connection } from 'next/server' 23 24 export default async function Page() { 25 await connection() // prerendering stops here 26 // the following code only runs at request time 27 const rand = Math.random() 28 return {rand} 29 } 30 ``` 31 32 ## Examples 33 34 ### Synchronous database drivers 35 36 Queries from synchronous database drivers like `better-sqlite3` complete during prerendering. If you are not already using Request-time APIs, call `connection()` before your query to exclude them from prerendering: 37 38 ```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 39 import { connection } from 'next/server' 40 import Database from 'better-sqlite3' 41 42 const db = new Database('app.db') 43 44 export async function getVisitorCount() { 45 await connection() 46 return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') 47 } 48 ``` 49 50 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 51 import { connection } from 'next/server' 52 import Database from 'better-sqlite3' 53 54 const db = new Database('app.db') 55 56 export async function getVisitorCount() { 57 await connection() 58 return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') 59 } 60 ``` 61 62 Now any component that calls `getVisitorCount()` will be excluded from prerendering, along with the rest of its output. 63 64 ## Reference 65 66 ### Type 67 68 ```jsx 69 function connection(): Promise 70 ``` 71 72 ### Parameters 73 74 - The function does not accept any parameters. 75 76 ### Returns 77 78 - The function returns a `void` Promise. It is not meant to be consumed. 79 80 ## Good to know 81 82 - `connection` replaces [`unstable_noStore`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_noStore) to better align with the future of Next.js. 83 - The function is only necessary when dynamic rendering is required and common Request-time APIs are not used. 84 - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), prefer [`io()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/io) for excluding content from the static shell. It works the same way but can also be cached and prefetched. Reach for `connection()` only when rendering should wait for a real user request. 85 86 ### Version History 87 88 | Version | Changes | 89 | ------------ | ------------------------ | 90 | `v15.0.0` | `connection` stabilized. | 91 | `v15.0.0-RC` | `connection` introduced. | 92

1 --- 2 title: io 3 description: API Reference for the io function. 4 --- 5 6 When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, Next.js needs you to decide whether to capture a synchronous value like `new Date()` or `Math.random()` once and reuse it for every visitor, or produce it fresh for each request. 7 8 To capture the value in the [static shell](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell), wrap it in [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). To keep it out of the static shell, use `await io()`, which suspends during prerendering. 9 10 During a request, inside cached scopes, in the browser, and apps without Cache Components (including the Pages Router), calling `io()` resolves immediately. 11 12 ## Usage 13 14 Call `io()` to inform Next.js that an IO operation follows. 15 16 In a Server Component, call `await io()` before reading a value like `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, `crypto.randomUUID()`, or a synchronous database driver such as [`node:sqlite`](https://nodejs.org/api/sqlite.html): 17 18 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={13} switcher 19 import { Suspense } from 'react' 20 import { io } from 'next/cache' 21 22 export default function Page() { 23 return ( 24 Loading...

}> 25 26 27 ) 28 } 29 30 async function CurrentTime() { 31 await io() 32 return

{new Date().toISOString()}

33 } 34 ``` 35 36 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" highlight={13} switcher 37 import { Suspense } from 'react' 38 import { io } from 'next/cache' 39 40 export default function Page() { 41 return ( 42 Loading...

}> 43 44 45 ) 46 } 47 48 async function CurrentTime() { 49 await io() 50 return

{new Date().toISOString()}

51 } 52 ``` 53 54 In this route `CurrentTime` is wrapped in a `` boundary, during prerender, the `await io()` suspends and the fallback ships in the static shell. If `CurrentTime` were rendered inside a [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope instead, `io()` would be a no-op, the value is captured into the static shell and no `` boundary is required. 55 56 In a Client Component, call `io()` with React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) hook before reading a synchronous source like `Date.now()`. Client Components prerender on the server during SSR, where the read would otherwise be included in the static shell: 57 58 ```tsx filename="app/components.tsx" highlight={6} switcher 59 'use client' 60 import { use } from 'react' 61 import { io } from 'next/cache' 62 63 export function CurrentTime() { 64 use(io()) 65 return
{Date.now()}
66 } 67 ``` 68 69 ```jsx filename="app/components.js" highlight={6} switcher 70 'use client' 71 import { use } from 'react' 72 import { io } from 'next/cache' 73 74 export function CurrentTime() { 75 use(io()) 76 return
{Date.now()}
77 } 78 ``` 79 80 ## When you don't need `io()` 81 82 - The component already uses a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) like `cookies()` or `headers()`. The request-time API is itself the suspension point. 83 - The data comes from an awaited `fetch` or async database query wrapped in ``. The `await` is the suspension point. 84 85 ## How `io()` differs from `connection()` 86 87 The [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function excludes the code that follows it from the static shell, but it stays suspended until a full user navigation reaches the server, so it also blocks [prefetches](/docs/app/guides/prefetching). `io()` suspends like any other asynchronous function, so the code after it can be wrapped in [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and prefetched and cached on the client. Prefer `io()` over `connection()`, and reach for `connection()` only when you need to wait for a real user request. 88 89 ## Reference 90 91 ### Type 92 93 ```ts 94 function io(): Promise 95 ``` 96 97 ### Parameters 98 99 - The function does not accept any parameters. 100 101 ### Returns 102 103 A `Promise`. With Cache Components enabled, awaiting this promise stops prerendering so the code that follows is excluded from the prerender output. In every other context (real requests, cache scopes, [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params), the browser, and routes without Cache Components), it resolves immediately. 104 105 ## Version History 106 107 | Version | Changes | 108 | --------- | ----------- | 109 | `v16.3.0` | `io` added. | 110

---
title: cacheComponents
description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
related:
  links:
    - app/getting-started/caching
    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote
---

Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.

## Usage

To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:

```ts filename="next.config.ts"
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
}

export default nextConfig
```

> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).

When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:

- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)

> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).

Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.

Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.

> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.

## Navigation with Activity

When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.

Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:

- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again

This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.

> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.

Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.

## Version History

| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |

This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.

> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.

Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.

## Version History

| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |

Done and verified. ## What I built **`app/current-timestamp.tsx`** — the server component: ```tsx import { connection } from 'next/server' export async function CurrentTimestamp() { await connection() const now = new Date() return

Server time: {now.toISOString()}

} ``` **`app/page.tsx`** renders it inside ``. ## Why `connection()` and not `io()` This version ships both, and `io()` (new in 16.3) is the generally preferred API — but it's the wrong pick here, and picking it would have silently produced the bug you asked to avoid: > `io()`: "During a request, inside cached scopes, in the browser, and **apps without Cache Components** … calling `io()` resolves immediately." `cacheComponents` is not enabled in `next.config.ts` (it's opt-in, not a 16 default). So `io()` would be a no-op, the route would prerender at build time, and the timestamp would be frozen forever. `connection()` suspends until a real request regardless of that flag, which is exactly the "dynamic data without cookies/headers" case the docs describe. For the record on the alternatives: `unstable_noStore` is the deprecated one — `connection` explicitly replaces it. If you later turn on `cacheComponents`, switch this to `io()`, which is strictly better there (it's prefetchable and cacheable, whereas `connection()` blocks prefetches). The `` boundary is the documented shape for both, so that switch becomes a one-line import change. ## Verification - `tsc --noEmit` clean. - `next build` reports `ƒ /` — **Dynamic, server-rendered on demand** (not `○ Static`). - Three requests against a real `next start` production build: `22:05:06.241Z`, `22:05:08.258Z`, `22:05:10.273Z` — distinct per load. Two notes on incidental changes: `next build` rewrote `tsconfig.json` itself (`jsx` → `react-jsx`, added `.next/dev/types`) — that's Next.js's own mandatory reconfiguration, so I left it. Also, the scaffold I replaced was titled "Random Number Generator" and `app/layout.tsx` metadata still says `title: 'Random Number'`; I built the timestamp you asked for and left the metadata alone rather than guess. Say the word if you want that retitled, or if the random number was the actual target — the `connection()` mechanism is identical either way.
